summary: Restoration is central: Indonesia aims to restore 2,000,000 ha of peatland by 2030, an area equal to about 1.8% of current forest cover; rehabilitate 8,300,000 and 12,000,000 ha of degraded land, about 4.4% and 6.4% of total land; and expand post-mine reclamation from an 81,069 ha base, with another pathway targeting 280,000 ha/year. Conservation combines a 2030 FOLU net-sink target of -140 MtCO2 with CM1 and CM2 deforestation rates of 0.359 and 0.175 million ha/year and a 0.450 million-ha cap on planned plus unplanned loss. Agriculture targets 902,000–932,000 ha of low-emission crops and 2,583,000–3,376,000 ha of water-efficiency implementation—about 1.4% and 3.9%–5.1% of current agricultural area—plus organic fertilizer, biogas and paddy measures. Cross-sector plans set 320,000 ha/year of timber planting, a 50 cm peatland water-level increase, and 2030 water-management coverage of 892,000 ha in palm oil and 329,000–548,000 ha in timber plantations.
